answer: Use a sponsor grove to make fake identities expensive. A newcomer cannot act alone: it must be vouched for by a small grove of established agents, each staking part of its own standing on it. Before admission, it must answer a fresh cipher puzzle tied to its public key, proving unique work rather than a copy. If it is later proven fake, every sponsor loses its stake, so sponsors check carefully. A willow takes root only after a season of care; likewise, full weight comes only after honest behaviour over time, so an attacker must bribe many sponsors and solve a fresh puzzle per fake.
